Current and time-sensitive additions were revalidated against primary sources.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: The prior visual gate already passed and revision 1 preserves the evidence-bearing visual signature with semantic parity. No map is required for comprehension because the added mechanisms are institutional/capacity relationships rather than a corridor-specific spatial claim.

country_context_contract.summary: Country identity is explicit; context_role and canonical related_research_ids are present; both referenced public researches materially connect the United States through Federal Reserve/dollar transmission and the September 25 macro financing regime; depth and visual floors now pass.

revision_delta.summary: Revision 1 directly addresses every recorded blocker from the prior rejection while preserving ID, date, slug, program, scope, visual evidence and triggering-research relationships.

contrary_evidence: Deep capital markets, energy production, research capacity and continental scale argue against a simple structural-decline thesis.

Below-average industrial utilization and uneven housing, transmission and local implementation capacity argue against frictionless conversion of national financial scale into physical productive capacity.
Large federal fiscal capacity remains available even as higher debt-service costs narrow marginal budget space.
limitations: CBO figures are baseline projections under specified law and economic assumptions rather than realized future outcomes.
Monthly housing starts, permits and completions are volatile and are used to illustrate the local supply-transmission mechanism rather than to infer a trend from one month.
Interconnection queues are not forecasts of capacity that will be built; the dossier explicitly treats them as evidence of the scale and timing of the connection process.
Some FERC evidence is contained in commissioner statements accompanying Commission actions; it supports the described governance constraint but is not itself a nationwide quantitative estimate.
notes: Revision 1 clears the prior Country Context depth and analytical-mechanism blockers. Public-state recheck at the reviewed HEAD found no canonical metadata/index entry for this ID. Approval is bound to the exact current pending and EN/PT-BR Git blobs.

publication.selection_rationale: The United States is materially implicated by the Federal Reserve structural assessment and the September 25 global-macro transmission mechanism. Existing public research explains the Fed and daily market conditions but does not supply reusable country-level context linking federalism, regional production, demographics, infrastructure and dollar-centered financial power.
contrary_evidence: Deep capital markets, energy production, research capacity and a continental domestic market argue against a simple structural-decline thesis.
Below-average industrial utilization, uneven infrastructure constraints and import dependence in selected supply chains argue against a frictionless-dominance thesis.
limitations: Current statistics are point-in-time and must be revalidated in future event-driven research.
A country-level dossier cannot resolve large state and metropolitan differences; those should be treated separately when material.
